newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria offered assistance by Zambia in mining.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria offered assistance by Zambia in mining.

text.p: Nigeria has been offered assistance by Zambia to help develop its mining sector, the national news agency reported on Tuesday.

"We have contacted the Nigerian ministry of solid minerals and the committee on solid minerals exploitation to offer our services," Lieutenant-Colonel Bizwayo Nkunika, acting Zambian high commissioner to Nigeria said, quoted by the News agency of Nigeria.
"Zambia would be willing to share its technical know-how and train Nigerians in our mining institutions," Nkunika added.
Nigeria's military government said in 1995 it was turning attention to solid minerals, among them coal and tin, to diversify the country's foreign exchange income.

Finance minister Anthony Ani said on Monday at a breakdown of the 1997 fiscal budget that Nigeria hoped to earn about 161 billion naira of its projected 404 billion naira this year from non-oil sources, including solid minerals.
Nkunika said Zambia has over 40 years mining experience and exploits solid minerals like cobalt, zinc, lead and copper, of which its mines are some of the world's largest.
